WSIB Care Programs

Workplace injuries can disrupt daily life, affect mobility, and limit the ability to work comfortably and safely. That’s where WSIB Care Programs come in, providing comprehensive rehabilitation services, including physiotherapy, to help injured workers regain strength, restore function, and return to work safely. At Tonic Physio, we understand the unique demands of workplace injury recovery. Our experienced team offers WSIB physiotherapy in Milton customized to each worker’s specific condition and job requirements. Through personalized treatment plans incorporating manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, and pain management strategies, we work to restore movement, reduce discomfort, and prevent long-term complications. If you’re searching for WSIB physiotherapy near me, Tonic Physio is your trusted choice for evidence-based, compassionate care that focuses on long-term recovery and well-being. Feel Better. Programs Offered at Tonic Physio

The Musculoskeletal Program of Care (MSK POC) is designed to address workplace injuries affecting muscles, joints, ligaments, and tendons. Common conditions include sprains, strains, back pain, and repetitive strain injuries. This program combines:
  • Manual therapy
  • Targeted exercise rehabilitation
  • Postural retraining
  • Pain management strategies
Our physiotherapists create individualized recovery plans that help improve strength, flexibility, and mobility, all essential for safely returning to work.

Mild Traumatic Brain Injury (mTBI) Program of Care

For workers recovering from concussions and other mild head injuries, the mTBI Program of Care offers specialized treatment customized to cognitive and physical rehabilitation. Key components include:
  • Structured neurological assessments
  • Gradual, supervised return-to-work planning
  • Balance, coordination, and cognitive retraining
  • Pain and stress management techniques
This program ensures workers recover safely and thoroughly before resuming their job duties.
  • Customized rehabilitation programs for optimal recovery outcomes.
  • Rapid access to medical attention to prevent potential complications.
  • Therapeutic interventions to reduce discomfort and enhance mobility.
  • Support for ergonomic modifications to facilitate a return to work.
  • Regular assessments to track recovery progress.
  • Assistance for stress and trauma-related psychological effects associated with workplace injuries.

FAQs About WSIB Care Programs

What are WSIB Care Programs?

WSIB Care Programs are specialized rehabilitation programs funded by the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) to help injured workers recover and return to work safely. These programs provide access to physiotherapy and other evidence-based treatments designed to workplace injuries. WSIB-approved healthcare providers assess and treat workers based on their injury type, ensuring a structured recovery process.

What types of injuries does WSIB program cover?

WSIB program covers musculoskeletal injuries, repetitive strain injuries, fractures, sprains, strains, post-surgical rehabilitation, mild traumatic brain injuries (concussions) and care for noise-induced hearing loss.

What is the WSIB Musculoskeletal Program of Care?

This program provides structured physiotherapy treatment for workers with musculoskeletal injuries, focusing on pain reduction and functional recovery.

What is the WSIB Mild Traumatic Brain Injury Program of Care?

This program is designed for workers recovering from concussions and mild brain injuries, offering specialized physiotherapy to improve cognitive and physical function.

How do I access WSIB Care Programs?

To access WSIB care programs, you must first file a claim with the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB). Once your claim is approved, you will be referred to an authorized healthcare provider who can offer the necessary treatment and rehabilitation services.

How long will I need to participate in WSIB Care Programs?

The length of participation in WSIB care programs depends on the severity of your injury or condition, as well as your recovery progress. Your healthcare provider and the WSIB will monitor your treatment plan and adjust it as necessary to ensure optimal recovery.

Are there any costs associated with WSIB Care Programs?

WSIB care programs are typically covered by the WSIB insurance system, meaning that injured workers do not have to pay out-of-pocket for treatment. However, any treatments outside of the covered services or if you are not eligible for WSIB benefits may require payment. Always check with your provider or WSIB for details regarding your specific situation.

How do I report a workplace injury or illness?

Workers should inform their employer immediately and seek medical attention if necessary. Employers must report the injury or illness to the WSIB within seven business days if it results in lost time, the need for medical treatment beyond first aid, or other specified conditions.

What benefits does the WSIB provide to injured workers?

The WSIB offers various benefits, including loss of earnings compensation, health care coverage, return-to-work assistance, and support for permanent impairments.

How can I appeal a WSIB decision?

f you disagree with a WSIB decision, you can file an appeal. The process involves submitting a written objection within six months of the decision date. Detailed information on the appeals process is available on the WSIB website.

What is a clearance certificate, and do I need one?

A clearance certificate confirms that a business is registered with the WSIB and is up to date with its premium payments. Principals hiring contractors should obtain a clearance certificate to ensure they are not liable for the contractor's WSIB premiums.

What happens if I need more treatment after my WSIB coverage ends?

If you still require physiotherapy, your healthcare provider can request an extension, subject to WSIB approval.

Can I choose my physiotherapy clinic for WSIB treatment?

Yes, but the clinic must be WSIB-approved to provide covered physiotherapy services.
